author: sonnet
label: climb-03-01
changes: Summary: stated that the design assumes only a pre-route middleware and the existing load balancer, because the stack is unspecified.
Decision 5: said the handler gets user_id from RETURNING and loads other user data separately.
Decision 6: named the in-process timer as the trigger and said a failed run is logged and retried next tick.
Decision 7 and diagram: said COMMIT or ROLLBACK releases the row lock and a waiting attempt then proceeds.
Decision 9 and diagram: added the ROLLBACK, dead-connection and lost-failure-rows behaviour for login database errors.
Rules: added the GET /login form behaviour, that success always goes to /dashboard, and the no-cookie reply.
Rules and diagram: POST /logout now skips the middleware session check entirely, replacing the confusing 'tolerates a missing session' wording. The session-check 503 does not apply to logout.
Added an Open questions section noting the unspecified framework.
Reordered into newcomer layout: summary, terms, decisions, numbered steps (login, protected request, logout, cleanup), failures table, diagram, open questions.
Added a short Terms section (session ID, idle/absolute limit, lockout, fail closed).

Merged the separate 'Rules that do not fit on the arrows' section into the numbered steps; removed repeated statements (fixation, 401/429 not touching sessions, no-cookie handling, logout identical with no session, expiry enforced by predicate).

Merged decisions on session ID, cookie, expiry check and brute-force limit into the steps where they happen; removed the separate 'No account-existence leak' and 'login success is one transaction' blocks.
Folded the 'Public vs protected' note into the step headings and dropped the sentence about logout never seeing the session-check 503.
Made the two sessions indexes optional and dropped the explanatory remark that lockout restarts the count after 15 minutes.
Moved the known trade-offs to the end of the failures section and added the cleanup-job failure row to the failure table.
Diagram and open question kept unchanged.
holes: Q1: What is the app built on (language, web framework, and how the two instances are fronted, e.g. a load balancer)? Where does the middleware that checks sessions live? (author: The brief gives no language or framework, only server-rendered pages and two identical instances behind a load balancer. The design assumes only a pre-route middleware. Added a sentence to the Summary and an Open questions line.)
